territorial_scope.description: The offence applies to publication in Singapore of online election advertising for Singapore parliamentary and presidential elections.

evidence.quote: the person publishes, or causes to be published, in Singapore any content

summary.short: Bill amending the Parliamentary Elections Act 1954 and Presidential Elections Act 1991 to make it an offence to publish online election advertising containing realistic, digitally generated or manipulated representations of a candidate saying or doing something they did not. Applies from a date set by ministerial Gazette notification.
summary.long: Bill No. 29/2024 (first read 9 September 2024) amends the Parliamentary Elections Act 1954 and Presidential Elections Act 1991. New ss 61MA and 42LA make it an offence to publish, or cause publication in Singapore of, online election advertising during an election period that shows a realistic audio, visual or audiovisual representation of a candidate saying or doing something they did not, created wholly or partly with digitally generated or manipulated content, where the publisher knew or ought reasonably to have known of the advertising. Defence: proof on a balance of probabilities of no knowledge and no reason to believe the representation was untrue. Exclusions: private electronic communications, authorised news agencies, and prescribed circumstances. Penalty: fine up to $1,000, imprisonment up to 12 months, or both. The Returning Officer's corrective-direction power is extended to these contraventions; candidates may request directions, and knowingly false requests are an illegal practice. Non-compliance with a direction carries a fine up to $1,000,000 for social media service providers, otherwise up to $1,000 and/or 12 months. The Returning Officer must publish a list of consenting candidates. Commencement by ministerial Gazette notification.

relations.note: Clause 2 inserts new section 28(1C) and sections 61MA and 61N(2) and (2A)-(2B) and amends sections 61N(1) and 61S(3) and the Part 3 Division 3 heading.
Clause 3 inserts new section 10(2A) and sections 42LA and 42M(2) and (2A)-(2B) and amends sections 42M(1) and 42R(3) and the Part 3 Division 2A Subdivision (3) heading.

relations.target_text: election advertising regulations (subsidiary rules; not identified in the document)
relations.note: New section 61MA(4)(c) excludes publishing in other circumstances prescribed by the election advertising regulations; new section 42LA(4)(c) contains the same reference. Regulations are not named or cited in the text.

notes: The document is the Bill as read the first time on 9 September 2024 (Bill No. 29/2024), not the enacted Act; the registry's Act 34 of 2024 and 'in_force' status are not verified from this text. Commencement is by ministerial notification in the Gazette; no date is stated. Clause 3(g) is printed out of order in the source layout (the 'replace' wording appears split across lines), so the exact replacement text should be checked against the enacted Act. Section 61MA and section 42LA are parallel provisions for the Parliamentary and Presidential elections; the candidate definitions differ by reference to sections 28(1C) and 10(2A).

thresholds.note: The bill contains no numeric cutoff that changes the legal treatment of a person, entity or product. The monetary figures ($1,000 and $1,000,000 fine maxima, and the 12-month imprisonment term) are penalty maxima recorded under enforcement, not thresholds. The $1,000,000 maximum applies to providers of a social media service by entity type rather than at a numeric cutoff. The deposit sum under section 28 is referenced but not stated, and the commencement date is left to ministerial notification.
